Guide

Wool & silk underwear: how to choose, wear and care for it

Why so many people in cold climates swear by wool & silk, and how to find the right layer for you.

Why wear natural fibres next to your skin?

The layer closest to your skin does the most work: it has to keep you warm, move moisture away and still feel comfortable for hours. Natural fibres like wool and silk do this better than most synthetics. They breathe, they regulate temperature, and they feel soft rather than clammy.

Wool, silk or a blend?

MaterialFeelsBest for
Wool & silk (85/15, 70/30)Warm, soft, no itchAutumn and winter, everyday base layer
Pure silk (100%)Light, smooth, cool to the touchSpring and summer, under fine blouses
Cotton, wool & silkSoft and breathableAll year, sensitive skin

Wool insulates even when it is slightly damp and handles moisture well, which is why it is the classic base layer for Nordic winters. Silk is one of the lightest natural fibres and feels very smooth. Blending a little silk into wool keeps the warmth but gives a softer, itch-free feel. We have 47 wool-blend styles and 9 pure silk styles.

Which style is right for you?

  • Camisoles: thin straps, invisible under shirts and dresses.
  • Tank tops: wider straps, more coverage and warmth on the shoulders.
  • Short-sleeve tops: a little extra warmth under knitwear.
  • Long-sleeve tops & turtlenecks: the warmest layer for the coldest days.
  • Bodysuits: stay tucked in for a smooth line.
  • Cardigans & boleros: soft layers to wear on top.

Finding your size

Our underwear comes in S, M and L and is designed to fit close to the body, like a second skin, so it disappears under your clothes. If you are between sizes or want a looser layer, choose the larger size. You can exchange sizes within 14 days.

How to care for wool & silk

  • Hand wash in cool water (max 30 °C) with a mild wool or silk detergent.
  • Skip fabric softener and bleach.
  • Don't wring. Press out water gently in a towel.
  • Dry flat, away from radiators and direct sunlight.
  • Air between wears. Wool freshens up naturally, so you need to wash it less often.

Always follow the care label on your garment.
